questions.question: A woodlouse curls into a tight ball when touched by a twig. Which characteristic of living things does this observation show?
options: Living things respond to changes in their surroundings.
Living things need air, food, and water to survive.
questions.explanation: This is an example of a living thing responding to a stimulus (touch) in its surroundings by protecting itself.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of matter?
questions.explanation: Air is matter because it has mass and occupies space; sunlight, shadows, and heat are not matter.

questions.question: A platypus lays eggs, but it is classified as a mammal because it __________.
options: has fur on its body and suckles its young with milk
questions.explanation: Even though the platypus lays eggs, it is still classified as a mammal because it has fur and produces milk for its young.

questions.question: Which of the following is a natural source of light?
questions.explanation: The Sun produces its own light (a natural luminous source), while the Moon only reflects sunlight.

questions.question: What is the main function of the roots of a plant?
options: To absorb water and mineral salts from the soil and anchor the plant
To trap sunlight and make food for the plant
questions.explanation: Roots absorb water and dissolved mineral salts from the soil, and anchor the plant firmly in the ground.

questions.question: When an ice cube is placed on a metal tabletop at room temperature, the ice cube melts because it __________.
options: gains heat from the warmer tabletop and surrounding air
questions.explanation: The ice cube melts because it gains heat from the warmer tabletop and surrounding air; 'coldness' does not flow — only heat does.

questions.question: Which of the following animals has a 4-stage life cycle?
questions.explanation: Mosquitoes undergo complete metamorphosis with a 4-stage life cycle: Egg -> Larva -> Pupa -> Adult.

questions.question: Which organ in the skeletal system protects the human brain?
questions.explanation: The skull is the bony structure that protects the brain.

questions.question: When the North pole of Magnet A is brought near Pole X of Magnet B, they push away (repel) each other. What pole is Pole X?
questions.explanation: Like poles repel each other. Since Magnet A's North pole repels Pole X, Pole X must also be a North pole.

questions.question: Four glass containers were set up: Container W (Food, water, no air — airtight lid); Container X (Food, no water, wire mesh lid — has air); Container Y (No food, no water, wire mesh lid — has air); Container Z (Food, water, wire mesh lid — has air). An identical grasshopper was placed into each container. In which container will the grasshopper survive the longest?
questions.explanation: Container Z has food, water, and air — all three basic needs — so the grasshopper will survive the longest there.

questions.question: When 100 ml of water is poured from a round flask into a tall rectangular container, what happens to its shape and volume?
options: Shape remains the same, volume remains 100 ml
Shape remains the same, volume decreases
questions.explanation: Liquids take the shape of their container, but their volume stays constant regardless of the container's shape.

questions.question: A goldfish is classified as a fish because it has __________.
options: moist skin and lives on land
fins, scales, and breathes through gills
questions.explanation: Fish have fins and scales, and they breathe using gills to extract oxygen from water.

questions.question: A shadow is formed when light __________.
options: passes through a clear glass window
is completely absorbed by the air
is blocked by an opaque or translucent object
questions.explanation: A shadow forms when an opaque or translucent object blocks light from passing through, creating a dark area behind it.

questions.question: A white balsam flower was placed in a beaker containing blue dye. After three hours, the petals of the flower turned blue. Which plant part was responsible for transporting the dye up to the flower?
questions.explanation: The stem contains tube-like structures (xylem) that transport water (and the dissolved dye) upward to the flower.

questions.question: What happens to a solid metal ball when it gains heat?
options: Its volume decreases and it contracts.
Its volume increases and it expands.
questions.explanation: When a solid gains heat, its particles vibrate more and move further apart, causing the solid to expand (increase in volume).

questions.question: At which stage of the mosquito's life cycle is it called a wriggler?
questions.explanation: The larva stage of a mosquito is commonly called a 'wriggler' because of how it moves in water.

questions.question: What is the main function of the human circulatory system?
options: To break down food into simple substances
To take in oxygen and remove carbon dioxide
To transport blood containing oxygen, water, and nutrients to all body parts
To protect internal organs from physical injury
questions.explanation: The circulatory system transports blood carrying oxygen, water, and nutrients to all parts of the body.

questions.question: A potted green plant placed near a closed window gradually grows towards the direction of the sunlight. This shows that the plant __________.
options: can move from one place to another
responds to changes in its surroundings
does not need water to grow
questions.explanation: Growing towards light (phototropism) shows that plants respond to changes such as light in their surroundings.

questions.question: A syringe is filled with 30 cm^3 of air. When the nozzle is sealed tightly and the plunger is pushed inward, the volume of air decreases to 20 cm^3. This experiment shows that air __________.
questions.explanation: The decrease in volume when pressure is applied shows that air (a gas) can be compressed into a smaller space.

questions.question: Which of the following features is shared by ALL adult insects?
options: Two body parts and eight legs
Three body parts and six legs
Three body parts and two pairs of wings
Four body parts and a hard shell
questions.explanation: All adult insects share three body parts (head, thorax, abdomen) and six legs, though not all have wings.

questions.question: Which of the following materials allows almost all light to pass through it?
questions.explanation: Clear glass is transparent and allows almost all light to pass through it.

questions.question: What happens if all the leaves are completely plucked off a healthy green plant?
options: The plant will grow taller immediately.
The roots will stop absorbing water instantly.
The plant cannot make food and will eventually die.
The stem will produce flowers right away.
questions.explanation: Without leaves, the plant cannot carry out photosynthesis to make food, and will eventually die from lack of nutrients.

questions.question: When a hot metal spoon is placed into a bowl of cold soup, what happens to the temperatures of the spoon and the soup after ten minutes?
options: The spoon becomes hotter, and the soup becomes colder.
The temperature of the spoon decreases, while the temperature of the soup increases.
Both the spoon and the soup become colder than the room.
questions.explanation: Heat flows from the hotter spoon to the colder soup until both reach a similar temperature — the spoon cools down while the soup warms up.

questions.question: What is the correct sequence of the life cycle of a flowering plant?
options: Seed -> Seedling -> Adult plant (bearing flowers and fruits)
questions.explanation: The correct life cycle sequence of a flowering plant is: Seed -> Seedling -> Adult plant (which bears flowers and fruits).

questions.question: Where does a young seedling get its food from before its green leaves appear?
options: From water absorbed through its root hairs
questions.explanation: Before true leaves appear, the seedling relies on stored food in its seed leaves (cotyledons) for nourishment.
